call.description: A recorded tool invocation. `to` references the tool, so a query names a tool by .call.to.tool.name=…; `name`, when present, is the name the caller wrote. Its outcome is not on the call: .execution.state beside it reads running, done, failed or interrupted, and what the tool answered is the result that names it (.result.call=<call>, result{call, ms, value}), refused or thrown when that result also wears refusal{code} or exception{type, value}.

name.description: optional: the tool's name as the caller wrote it, which says what was asked for where `to` names a tool nobody serves, as a model's call to a tool it invented does

id.description: the provider's id for it, echoed in the result

args.description: its arguments: the object the tool's input schema describes

source.description: optional: the request or other entity this call came from

actor.description: The by/via identity pair of whoever last changed the executable request. Server-owned; an empty pair means automation. When absent, the creation author still owns the request.

cut.description: on a call: its writer stopped before its arguments were finished, as a model's reply cut at its output token limit does; it never runs, and its refusal (code cut) says why

result.description: What a tool returned, and how long the call took.

ms.description: how long the tool took, in milliseconds

call.description: the call it is the result of

value.description: what the tool answered as data, the `output{value}` beside its words, kept on the result where a reader of the transcript finds it

content.description: Text content, retained with the call that asked for it.

output.description: What produced the text beside it: the request, for a model’s own output, or the call whose failure is being reported. Only output carries it — text a person or a system wrote has none.

id.description: the provider's id for this piece of output, as `call.id` is its id for the call — what a later revision of the same item is matched on

value.description: the same output as data, for a reader that parses rather than reads: a tool that declares an outputSchema answers its structured content here, beside the text a person reads

images.description: Images returned beside the text and structured value, each with base64 bytes and a media type; an MCP client displays these as image content blocks.

refusal.description: A deliberate no: the tool or provider refused the request. Never tracked; its prose is on the content component beside it.

code.description: the tool or provider's reason for refusing

exception.description: What was thrown, retained in an answer or transcript entry. The catcher reports the original failure to the tracker separately.

execution.description: Who holds a recorded tool invocation; its state is computed from the interruption mark and explicitly named answers.

state.description: The lifecycle derived from its interruption mark, holder and recorded answers.

by.description: the server or process running it

tool.description: A registered tool that callers can invoke.

name.description: what callers call it; the entity id is derived from it

title.description: what a person reads in place of the name: an imperative phrase, such as Read or write app files

step.description: how a call reads to a person, as locale strings: doing while it runs (Texting %{person}…) and done once it answered (Texted %{person}), each %{name} filled from the call's arguments and the person it works for; under by, by argument then its value ('' when left out), the step of each thing the arguments choose

revision.description: implementation revision used by builders to detect changed code

call_ready.description: a call nobody has claimed and nobody scheduled: run the tool it names and attach the result. A call written already claimed (the caller runs it) owes nothing, and nor does one its writer runs by an effect of its own (`tool_async`, @yaks/session): that effect runs it with the tools its writer offered. In a graph that does not load the word, every unclaimed call is due

call_woken.description: Run a scheduled call when its wake writes fired, if the call has no result. In a graph without wake components, call_ready handles every unclaimed call.

finding.description: What a check measured: fail for a violated contract, warn for a leak or a verdict it could not establish.

tool.description: A registered tool that callers can invoke.
